6.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
6.text: "I flew in all the way from the Archipelago, just to be here today."

9.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
9.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)) == false

10.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
10.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn09_RumburgPeaceSummit_StartTalks"] == true) == false)

11.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
11.text: "I was in Rumburg a few days ago to meet with several energy industry leaders."
11.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn09_RumburgPeaceSummit_StartTalks"] == true)

15.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
15.text: "When you promised me you wouldn't tighten the Energy Protection Act, I had the feeling you wouldn't keep your word."
15.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Confrontation_USP_EnergyAct_RevertedTo10"]) and (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_PromiseNotHarsherEPA"] == true)

16.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
16.text: "I was in Rizia a few days ago to meet with our energy partners."

18.speaker: Player
18.text: "Colonel Soll is right about this. You did sell your shares to them and abandon Sordland to go live in their country."

22.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
22.text: "Did you know that the Anrakan Federation is building islands in the middle of the ocean?"

23.speaker: Tarquin Soll
23.text: "You shouldn't have. You don't live in Sordland anymore."

24.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
24.text: "I thought you would be happy to see an old friend."

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: Ewald's upper lip curled, but he quickly turned it into a smile.

26.speaker: Tarquin Soll
26.text: "I thought you couldn't sink any deeper when you handed the Anrakans the keys to our energy. But moving there was an all-time low, even for you."

27.speaker: Tarquin Soll
27.text: "Don't make me laugh, Ewald. You traded Sordland for damn Anraka."

28.speaker: Player
28.text: "Honestly, I feel the same way. This was not what I had in mind when I removed the Energy Protection Act."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: "Yes, Mr. Alphonso. Why did you decide to move to the Federation of Anrakan Isles?"

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "A former Sordish president who chose to retire on an island. Sounds familiar."

31.speaker: Tarquin Soll
31.text: "I chose to remain in Sordland, Mr. Rayne. My homeland. Not to sell myself off to the highest bidder."

32.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
32.text: "Gentlemen, please. Neither of you can judge me."

33.speaker: Tarquin Soll
33.text: "To live as a king, off of the backs of hard-working Sords."

34.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
34.text: "Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

35.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
35.text: "Mr. President, the state's investment in Gasom helped the company get back on its feet. I'll always appreciate that."

36.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
36.text: "But after you removed the EPA, the Anrakans made me the deal of a lifetime. I couldn't exactly refuse."

37.speaker: Player
37.text: "Let me guess. You live on one of them."

39.speaker: Player
39.text: "Is that why you sold Gasom to them and abandoned Sordland for Anraka?"

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "Why are you even here, Mr. Alphonso? You're not invested in the future of Sordland, so I can't imagine you're invested in Sordish football."

41.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
41.text: "Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

42.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
42.text: "Your hefty investment in Gasom helped the company get back on its feet. I'll always appreciate that."

43.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
43.text: "But after you removed the Energy Protection Act, the Anrakans made me the deal of a lifetime. I couldn't exactly refuse."

44.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
44.text: "I'm getting old. Surely I've earned the right to a comfortable retirement."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "I'd rather not discuss this any further, Mr. Alphonso."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "You persuaded the Sordish state to invest in Gasom as a leap of faith -- and then you turned around and sold your own shares."

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "Don't try to blame me for your own selfishness."

48.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
48.text: "Mr. Soll, please. You are not in a position to judge us."

50.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
50.text: "It's the perfect retirement. An entire island just for myself and my loved ones. And it's not even that expensive."

51.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
51.text: "Imagine your very own miniature paradise, with its topography custom-designed to suit your needs. Well, I don't need to imagine it -- I own one now."

52.speaker: Player
52.text: "That reminds me of another former president who lived on an island. Tarquin Soll."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: "Isn't that all a bit much? No need to be such a show-off."

60.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
60.text: "And now Gasom is booming. We've all won."

61.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
61.text: "We've all benefited, just like I said. You, me, Gasom and Sordland."

66.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
66.text: "Believe it or not, the Rumburgians are now talking about pursuing a friendlier relationship with Sordland."

67.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
67.text: "Selling my Gasom shares to Rumburg surely must have aided with this diplomatic achievement."

71.speaker: Tarquin Soll
71.text: "How dare you, son. If we avoided war with Rumburg, it was by the skin of our teeth, not because you handed the Queen the key to our energy grid."

72.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
72.text: "Thanks to President Rayne, Sordland and Rumburg are set to become allies and business partners. Old enemies can still be future friends, Mr. Soll."

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: Ewald's upper lip curled, but he quickly turned it into a smile.

74.speaker: Tarquin Soll
74.text: "And now you're even boasting about how you climbed into bed with our enemies."

75.speaker: Tarquin Soll
75.text: "Don't speak like an idiot, Ewald. You made this deal long before diplomacy with Rumburg was in the cards."

76.speaker: Tarquin Soll
76.text: "Yet you did it anyway, knowing that war might be on the horizon. Just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Soll is right about this. Rumburg should never have ended up with the largest share in Gasom."

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "Ewald, I must remind you that you sold those shares before any diplomatic talks were being discussed. Don't use that as an excuse."

79.speaker: Player
79.text: "I don't begrudge Mr. Alphonso his decision. Especially since our relations with Rumburg have improved so much."

80.speaker: Player
80.text: "He has the freedom to sell his personal assets to anyone he chooses. Including Rumburg."

81.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
81.text: "And Gasom is operating the same as ever. You don't even notice the difference in ownership."

82.speaker: Player
82.text: "Same as ever? It's a foreign-owned company and Rumburg has the biggest stake."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "That's good to hear. We can't risk any deterioration of relations with Rumburg."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "I must remind you that you sold those shares before any diplomatic talks were being discussed. You handed our largest rival the keys to our energy grid."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "How can you casually bring this up? You sold off Gasom, just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

86.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
86.text: "Mr. Rayne, please. You are not in a position to judge me."

87.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
87.text: "You didn't invest enough to help keep my company afloat, while opening the door to foreigners who were willing to do exactly that. What did you think would happen?"

88.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
88.text: "Rumburg and Rizia were never my first choices. But they came to Gasom's rescue when Sordland would not."

89.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
89.text: "I thought you'd be glad, Mr. Rayne. If your goal is to avoid conflict with Rumburg, a stake in Gasom is one hell of a peace offering."

90.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
90.text: "Gentlemen, please. Neither of you can judge me."

97.speaker: Tarquin Soll
97.text: "Why don't you also go ahead and sell FC Anrica to Queen Beatrice?"

98.speaker: Tarquin Soll
98.text: "Why don't you also go ahead and sell your shares of Underhall Construction to Queen Beatrice."

99.speaker: Tarquin Soll
99.text: "I can't believe the two of you. You join my party and then undermine everything it stands for."

100.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
100.text: "Exactly. And you are doing an extraordinary job on that front."

101.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
101.text: "Mr. Soll, please. You are in no position to judge us."

102.speaker: Tarquin Soll
102.text: "No, but history will judge you. And I suspect it will find you wanting."

104.speaker: Tarquin Soll
104.text: "You cannot trust a monarchy, gentlemen. Rizia and Rumburg will never be our friends."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "You should have been able to fix Gasom on your own, not go begging for investment."

107.speaker: Player
107.text: "Don't try to blame me for your own selfishness. I see now why Soll never trusted you."

108.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
108.text: "I did everything I could do on my own. But a company needs investors to truly thrive. Look at how it's been booming with Rumburg's involvement."

109.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
109.text: "We're putting stock in the old man's opinion now?"

110.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
110.text: "I've been starting to regret selling my Gasom shares to Rumburg."

114.speaker: Tarquin Soll
114.text: "Relations? We are on the verge of war, Mr. Alphonso."

115.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
115.text: "I had no idea our relations would sink this low."

116.speaker: Tarquin Soll
116.text: "You handed our enemies the keys to our energy. And now you're acting as if you had no idea Rumburg posed a threat."

117.speaker: Tarquin Soll
117.text: "You are a traitor. It's that simple."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "Don't make me laugh. You always knew that Rumburg posed a threat. But you cared more about your precious free market than national security."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "This is my fault as much as it is yours. I never should have removed the Energy Protection Act."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "Sink this low? War is upon us, Ewald. And you betrayed our nation by handing our enemies the keys to our energy."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "Don't expect me to sympathize with you. You sold off Gasom, just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

123.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
123.text: "I gave Sordland the first chance at a large investment. I told you that completely removing the Energy Protection Act might compromise our interests."

128.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
128.text: "When it was clear that Sordland wouldn't help Gasom, I had to look elsewhere. But I didn't hand Rumburg the key to Sordish energy, Mr. President. You did."

130.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
130.text: "I didn't know our relations would sink this low."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "Colonel Soll is right. You are a traitor, Ewald."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "What's done is done. Let's not start an argument."

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Don't expect anyone to sympathize with you. You sold off Gasom, just to line your pockets with Rumburgian crowns."

137.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
137.text: "Gentlemen, please. Let's not go that far."

138.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
138.text: "I did tell you not to raise the cap on foreign ownership over 49 percent, didn't I?"

139.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
139.text: "But please let's not dwell on this any longer. I just wanted to be open with you about it."

140.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
140.text: "I gave Sordland every chance to invest, didn't I? When you wouldn't help keep Gasom afloat, I had to look elsewhere."

144.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
144.text: "You ignored both of those pieces of advice, and went on to declare war on Rumburg."

145.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
145.text: "I can't believe you would attempt to follow in Soll's footsteps."

149.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
149.text: "Especially after you... brought him down like that."

152.speaker: Tarquin Soll
152.text: "When I passed the Energy Protection Act, my intention was to protect the Sordish state from nefarious interests. Not for the Sordish state to become one of those interests."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: "I was only trying to follow in your footsteps, Colonel."

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "Mr. Soll is right. You are always looking for someone else to blame, Ewald."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "What's done is done. Let's not start an argument now."

157.speaker: Player
157.text: "It wasn't my intention to revert it. The party forced me to do it. I had to compromise."

158.speaker: Player
158.text: "Don't be so harsh on him. I should have seen this coming."

162.speaker: Tarquin Soll
162.text: "No need to sympathize with him, Mr. Rayne.""

163.speaker: Tarquin Soll
163.text: "You should never have tried to go against the USP in the first place."

164.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
164.text: "You're right. Let's not dwell on this."

165.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
165.text: "Gentlemen, please. Let's not go that far."

167.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
167.text: "Okay, gentlemen. Let's not ponder over this any longer. My intention was not to start an argument."

168.speaker: Player
168.text: "Justice for Soll's oppression has nothing to do with his energy policies, Ewald."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "What's done is done. Let's not start an argument now."

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "The party forced me to revert your amendment to the EPA. I had to compromise."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "You may be right. I should have seen this coming."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "Don't try to pin your own failures on me."

178.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
178.text: "You should have. Because I warned you."

179.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
179.text: Anyway... Let's not dwell on this any longer. My intention was not to start an argument."

181.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
181.text: "I was happy to find out that the royals over there appear to be in favor of pursuing friendlier relations with Sordland."

182.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
182.text: "I still don't think they will do anything to harm their connection with Rumburg, but cooperating with them was the right call."

186.speaker: Tarquin Soll
186.text: "You're fond of the monarchists now, Ewald? They must be filling your pockets with Rizian gold."

187.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
187.text: "For Dast's sake, Mr. Soll, try to see the positive in what I do. For once."

191.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
191.text: "After all, thanks to them, Gasom is still up and running."
191.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Prison"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Death"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true) == false)

192.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
192.text: "Thanks to their joint investment with our government, Gasom is still up and running."

193.speaker: Player
193.text: "Thanks to the investment that *I* approved, you mean."

194.speaker: Player
194.text: "It's good to see that the strategy we came up is paying off."

195.speaker: Player
195.text: "It's good to see the positive results of their investment."

196.speaker: Player
196.text: "And what do you think about our Rizian partners?"

197.speaker: Player
197.text: "Let's not forget, Ewald. Rizia isn't doing this for charity."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "I still wouldn't rely on a kingdom -- one that has close ties with Queen Livingston especially."

199.speaker: Tarquin Soll
199.text: "How about you claim responsibility for once? It is your fault that a giant like Gasom was brought to the brink of collapse."

200.speaker: Tarquin Soll
200.text: "Admit it. It was too much of a responsibility for you. A man with your profit-focused mentality should have never been given the keys to such a vital sector."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "Mr. Soll is not wrong. You are always looking for someone else to blame, Ewald."

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "What's done is done, Mr. Soll. Let's not start an argument now."

205.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
205.text: "You're right. Let's not dwell on this."

206.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
206.text: "Gentlemen, please. Let's not go that far."

210.speaker: Player
210.text: "To be fair, it's good to see the positive results of our investment."

211.speaker: Player
211.text: "To be fair, it's good to see the positive results of their investment."

212.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
212.text: "A curious bunch, but they do know the gas business."

213.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
213.text: "They are an important regional player, Mr. Rayne. One that we should keep close to us."

214.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
214.text: "Oh. And they have great food and wine. Spend some time there and you'll realize how overrated Lespian cuisine is."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
215.text: "Truth be told, it was an incredible help."

217.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
217.text: "You are right to have your reservations but they are reliable business partners."

220.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
220.text: "Truth be told, it was an incredible help."

221.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
221.text: "I'm getting old, gentlemen. Surely I've earned the right to a comfortable retirement."

222.speaker: Tarquin Soll
222.text: "You and Mr. Rayne have earned nothing but my disdain."

223.speaker: Tarquin Soll
223.text: "Together, you are living proof of the dangers of Alphonsonomics and the free market."

227.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
227.text: "You recouped your investment, didn't you? The leap of faith was justified."

228.speaker: Player
228.text: "This isn't the fault of the free market. It's Mr. Alphonso's own selfishness."

229.speaker: Player
229.text: "You're right, Colonel. I see now that your energy protection laws were put in place for a reason."

230.speaker: Player
230.text: "'Dangers' would be overblown. Sordland and Gasom have both benefited from this deal."

231.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
231.text: "If you had your way and the EPA remained unchanged, Gasom would have gone bankrupt and thousands of good Sordish men and women would be out of work."

232.speaker: Tarquin Soll
232.text: "You're the one who ran Gasom into the ground, Mr. Alphonso. You should not have had to ask for foreign assistance in the first place."

233.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
233.text: "If I may gently remind you, it was never my intention to do away with the EPA altogether. That was a pure Anton Rayne touch."

234.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
234.text: "His laws as written would have choked the life out of Gasom. But I did see the wisdom in putting a cap on foreign ownership. You're the one who wanted to do away with it entirely."

235.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
235.text: "Indeed. The value of Sordland's investment has only gone up since the Anraka purchase."

236.speaker: Tarquin Soll
236.text: "And you, Mr. Rayne. By overturning my Energy Protection Act, you set the stage for exactly this."

240.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
240.text: "Besides which, the value of Sordland's own shares in Gasom has never been higher."

241.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
241.text: "And surely you knew this might happen when you removed the Energy Protection Act."

242.speaker: Player
242.text: "No, I was naive enough to think all your talk about protecting your legacy meant you'd hold on to your shares."

243.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
243.text: "Absolutely not. But now that they own such a large stake in Gasom, they would never damage its value by provoking conflict."

247.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
247.text: "And the value of Sordland's own shares in Gasom has never been higher. This is truly a win-win solution for everyone."

248.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
248.text: "I do wish you had taken me up on my offer. Sordland would have more than recouped its investment by now."

249.speaker: Player
249.text: "I'm glad about that. Our co-investment with Rizia was the right call in the end."

250.speaker: Player
250.text: "All right. The next time you offer me a deal, I'll take it."

251.speaker: Player
251.text: "I still don't feel entirely comfortable that Rumburg has so much leverage over us."

252.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
252.text: "To be honest, neither do I. That's why I never advocated for the complete removal of the Energy Protection Act."

253.speaker: Player
253.text: "I didn't count on Rumburg ending up with the largest stake in Gasom, no."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "I still think not investing was the right call. It wasn't up to Sordland to fix Gasom's mess."

255.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
255.text: "Oh, I'm out of the deal-making business these days. You're better off asking Gus."

256.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
256.text: "It doesn't make a difference to me. Just pointing out that we both could have struck it rich."

257.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
257.text: "As long as Rizia, Rumburg and Sordland all remain on friendly terms, it'll be smooth sailing."

258.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
258.text: "My legacy is my company, Mr. Rayne. My shares are meaningless if the company stagnates."

259.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
259.text: "President Rayne, you didn't invest enough to help keep my company afloat, while opening the door to foreigners who were willing to do exactly that. What did you think would happen?"

260.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
260.text: "Rumburg and Rizia were never my first choices. But they came to Gasom's rescue when Sordland would not."

261.speaker: Tarquin Soll
261.text: "They would not even have had that opportunity if you two hadn't begun meddling with the Energy Protection Act."

262.speaker: Tarquin Soll
262.text: "Together, you are living proof of the dangers of Alphonsonomics and the free market."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: "This isn't the fault of the free market. It's Mr. Alphonso's own selfishness."

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "You're right, Colonel. I see now that your energy protection laws were put in place for a reason."

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
265.text: "I will say that I never advocated for the complete removal of the EPA. That was purely Anton Rayne's decision."

266.speaker: Player
266.text: "Don't blame me for your own selfishness."

267.speaker: Player
267.text: "Let's not play the blame game. We have to focus on the here and now."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: "I removed the EPA as a favor to Gasom. And you returned that favor by selling your shares to our enemy."

269.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
269.text: "I never asked for the removal of the EPA. I wanted to put Sordish interests first."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "This is my fault, Colonel. I never should have removed the Energy Protection Act."

274.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
274.text: "I had a feeling that despite all of our conversations, you never truly grasped how much Gasom meant to me or Sordland."

278.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
278.text: "But removing the EPA for just long enough to maximize the value of your investment, then selling your shares before forcing our foreign investors to sell theirs and bankrupting our company?"

279.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
279.text: "You're a snake, Rayne. Pure and simple."

280.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
280.text: "But I hope you see now how much damage you've done to our country's energy industry."

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "It was never my intention to bankrupt Gasom. I made my decisions with the company's interests at heart."

285.speaker: Player
285.text: "I was forced to revert the EPA to 10 percent foreign ownership. The USP made me do it."

286.speaker: Tarquin Soll
286.text: "Blaming the USP for your own mistakes. That's an Ewald Alphonso move if I ever heard of one."

287.speaker: Tarquin Soll
287.text: "My footsteps? If it were up to me, Gasom would have been nationalized long ago to prevent exactly this from happening."

288.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
288.text: "Excuse me, but that's bullshit and you know it."

289.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
289.text: "Leave me out of this. I've only ever tried to do what's right for Sordland."

290.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
290.text: "All you had to do was leave your investment and the EPA untouched, Mr. Rayne. But that somehow proved too difficult for you."

291.speaker: Narrator
291.text: The three of us glared at each other.

292.speaker: Player
292.text: "It was never my intention to bankrupt Gasom. I made my decisions with the company's interests at heart."

293.speaker: Player
293.text: "I was forced to revert the EPA to 10 percent foreign ownership. The USP made me do it."

294.speaker: Player
294.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. Alphonso. But you got through it all unscathed, didn't you?"

295.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
295.text: "Of course I did. But Gasom is as much a part of my legacy as my presidency. And now it's been tainted forever."

296.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
296.text: "Do not blame your own shortcomings on your party, Mr. President."

297.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
297.text: "Excuse me, but that is bullshit and you know it."

302.speaker: Tarquin Soll
302.text: "What are you talking about, Alphonso? I've read the reports. Your Gasom is doing fine without foreign investment propping it up."

303.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
303.text: "We are barely turning a profit. All it would take is a bad few months for it all to come crashing down."

304.speaker: Tarquin Soll
304.text: "You cannot lay your own failures at the feet of the state, Alphonso."
304.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Prison"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Death"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Gasom_Default"] == true) == false)

305.speaker: Tarquin Soll
305.text: "Admit it. A man with your profit-focused mentality should have never been given the keys to such a vital sector, let alone the presidency."

306.speaker: Tarquin Soll
306.text: "Then that is your fault. Not the Sordish state's."
